reason: Writer wrappers gate only on WriterActive() (= any sampled request in the process, internal/taint/propagation/writer.go:23-25), so every Builder/Buffer op in every goroutine runs updateWriter while any owner is active. updateWriter zeroes a 6312-byte Snapshot and calls LookupWriterValue, which walks 64 owner records 187 KB apart plus writerPresent. Buffer does this twice, and Reset/String/WriteByte/WriteRune/Grow do it too, although the result is a no-op for clean input without writer state. Woven customer code: about 16.3 us/op vs about 0.31 us/op unwoven (about 50x). Internal API on Go 1.27.0: hook 1025 vs gated 117 ns (Builder), 1470 vs 65 ns (Buffer). The existing HasWriterStates/MayContain gate preserves provenance. Only the one-allocation writer anchor is documented as accepted.
